topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides introductory framing for the lecture, noting the complexity and historical context of complement.

topics.label: Foundations and Core Mechanics of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition mechanisms that drive C3 deposition and converge on the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector functions through which activated complement destroys pathogens and coordinates immune clearance.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in specific complement components produce distinct clinical diseases and infection susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the strategies evolved by pathogens to evade complement destruction, focusing on Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
